```{r a1-setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7,
  fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 120, out.width = "100%")
options(width = 82)
```

We consider the assignment of six sites to ordered groups when their scores
are uncertain. A complete ranking specifies a direction for every pair.
In postrank, comparisons may instead be withheld by assigning sites to
the same grade. The loss balances posterior expected wrong-direction errors against the
cost of withholding. This formulation
applies to one criterion or to several criteria.

The analysis first uses one score and then includes a second score for the
same sites. Grade 1 has highest priority. A shared grade withholds the
comparison between two sites without asserting equality of their scores.

## Posterior input {#begin-with-a-small-posterior-input}

```{r a1-load}
library(postrank)
sites <- pr_tutorial
```

The example comprises six fictional sites, A through F, with specified
score means and standard deviations. Each score has a normal distribution
with standard deviation 0.2 in illustrative standardized units. Sites are
independent, as are the two scores within a site. Higher scores receive
higher priority on both criteria. These distributions define a teaching
example; they are not fitted to observations from actual sites.

`sites$one` contains the first score. `sites$two` adds the second score
while retaining the same distribution for the first. Both inputs contain
analytic comparison probabilities and the information required for marginal
posterior intervals. In an application, the targets, directions and
dependence assumptions must first be specified, as described in
[Analysis of supplied posterior results](a5-your-posterior-results.html).

```{r a1-law}
knitr::kable(data.frame(Site = sites$units$label, sites$law$means),
  row.names = FALSE, digits = 2,
  col.names = c("Site", "Score A mean", "Score B mean"))
```

## Loss and grade constraints {#choose-what-the-first-report-should-say}

The first analysis specifies two reporting choices. `G_max = 3` permits
at most three grades, including solutions with fewer grades. `tau = 0.2` is
the loss incurred by withholding a pair, whereas an incorrect disclosed
direction has loss one before averaging over pairs. Decreasing `tau`
therefore reduces the relative cost of withholding. The supported range is
`0 < tau <= 0.5`.

The following call computes the analysis using HiGHS and requires the
optional `highs` package. It is displayed without execution. The results and
figures below use prepared analyses obtained with the same calls and inputs;
consequently, rendering this article does not require an optimizer.

```{r a1-one-call, eval=FALSE}
one <- postrank(sites$one, tau = 0.2, G_max = 3, backend = "highs",
  control = postrank_control(time_limit = 60, threads = 1, seed = 1304))
```

```{r a1-prepared, include=FALSE}
source(system.file("scripts", "_vignette-setup.R", package = "postrank",
  mustWork = TRUE), local = TRUE)
one <- load_or_compute("tutorial_one")
two <- load_or_compute("tutorial_two")
ev1 <- one$fit$evaluation; ev2 <- two$fit$evaluation
fmt <- function(x, digits = 4) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits)
```

For a single criterion, the criterion weight is automatically one, so the
loss involves no averaging across criteria.

```{r a1-one-result}
one
```

The result uses `r ev1$G` grades and discloses `r ev1$N` of the
`r ev1$M` possible pairs. Sites A and B are assigned to grade 1, C and D to
grade 2, and E and F to grade 3. Since A has a smaller grade number than C,
the report places A above C. The comparison of A with B is withheld; their
order of presentation within the grade has no inferential interpretation.

The posterior expected number of errors among disclosed pairs is
`r fmt(ev1$E[[1]], 3)`. Dividing by the `r ev1$N` disclosed pairs yields
`r fmt(ev1$E_over_N[[1]])` expected errors per disclosed pair. This average
summarizes the selected directions; individual pairs may have different
posterior error probabilities.

The loss also includes the cost of the `r ev1$M - ev1$N` withheld pairs:

```{r a1-risk}
p <- get_profile(one)
(p$E + 0.2 * (15 - 12)) / 15
get_risk(one)
```

The resulting loss is `r fmt(ev1$primary_risk)`. Assigning all sites to a
single grade would withhold every comparison and give loss 0.2 under this
loss definition. Expected errors per disclosed pair would then be undefined,
since the denominator would be zero. A report can therefore disclose
selected directions while withholding the remaining comparisons.

The prepared result includes a small floating-point correction to the
solver bound. The reported lower bound exceeded the independently evaluated
action loss by an amount within the numerical tolerance. The recorded gap is
zero after correction. This gap concerns optimization conditional on the
supplied probabilities; it provides neither a measure of posterior
uncertainty nor model validation. The warning and further details are
retained in `summary(one)`.

## Posterior summaries and grades {#read-estimates-alongside-grades}

```{r a1-one-card, fig.cap="Six fictional sites: score A means and 90% equal-tail marginal posterior intervals. Higher scores have higher priority; the grade strips show which comparisons are withheld."}
postrank_plot_report_card(one,
  entity_labels = setNames(sites$units$label, sites$units$entity_id),
  criterion_labels = c(score_A = "Score A (standardized units)"))
```

The points and marginal 90% intervals describe scores under the specified
normal laws, whereas the grade strips represent the selected comparisons.
The intervals have neither simultaneous coverage across sites nor an
interpretation as intervals for grade labels. Interval overlap alone cannot
recover the grading decision, which also depends on the withholding cost
and grade cap. The complete grade table is available through
`as.data.frame(one)`, and the named grade vector through `get_grades(one)`.

## Analysis with two criteria {#add-a-second-criterion}

We next include score B. Although sites C and D have lower score A means
than A and B, their score B means exceed that of B. A common grading must
therefore accommodate different directions of comparison. We assign equal
weights to the criteria and retain the withholding cost and grade cap.

```{r a1-two-call, eval=FALSE}
two <- postrank(sites$two,
  weights = c(score_A = 0.5, score_B = 0.5),
  tau = 0.2, G_max = 3, backend = "highs",
  control = postrank_control(time_limit = 60, threads = 1, seed = 1304))
```

```{r a1-two-result}
as.data.frame(two)
get_profile(two)[, c("criterion", "weight", "E", "E_over_N", "risk")]
```

The common report assigns A through D to grade 1, E to grade 2 and F to
grade 3. It discloses `r ev2$N` of `r ev2$M` pairs and withholds
`r ev2$M - ev2$N`. The criterion-specific error profiles differ despite
equal weights. The weights determine contributions to expected loss, rather
than requiring equal error rates.

```{r a1-two-card, fig.height=4.8, fig.cap="The same sites with two criteria: 90% marginal intervals in illustrative standardized units. Both panels use one common grading; higher score values have higher priority in each panel."}
postrank_plot_report_card(two,
  entity_labels = setNames(sites$units$label, sites$units$entity_id),
  criterion_labels = c(score_A = "Score A (standardized units)",
    score_B = "Score B (standardized units)"))
```

The change in grouping results from including the second criterion while
holding the first score's distribution fixed. The two scalar losses average
errors over different sets of criteria and therefore cannot be interpreted
as competing measures of accuracy. Comparisons of alternative gradings
require evaluation under common posterior inputs, weights and withholding
cost.

The posterior support for a disclosed direction may differ between criteria,
even though both use the same grades. Criterion-specific expected errors
are therefore relevant to assessing the common report. Applications are
given for [school chronic absence](a2-cde-accountability.html), with one
criterion, [race and gender at employers](a3-krw-race-gender.html), and
[income and incarceration in Alabama](a4-alabama-opportunity.html).
[Reading and exporting results](a6-reading-exporting-results.html) describes
the result tables and computation states, while
[Figures and sensitivity analysis](a7-figures-sensitivity.html) examines
changes in weights, costs and grade caps.

The methodological articles explain the [one-criterion loss and its KRW correspondence](m1-ranking-and-loss.html) and the [different goals available with several criteria](m2-several-criteria.html).
